study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Data were acquired from a single site: the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University. All participants (98 OCD patients and 130 healthy controls) were recruited from this site. The normative model was trained on the 130 healthy controls from this single site. MRI scans were acquired using a 3T GE Discovery MR750 scanner.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Ninety-eight first-episode and drug-naive patients with OCD were recruited from outpatient services of the Department of Psychiatry, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University." "One hundred and thirty healthy controls (HCs) were recruited from the community through poster advertisement." "T1-weights MRI scans were acquired using 3-Tsela GE Discovery MR750 scanner (General Electric, Fairfield Connecticut, USA) at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Methods / Sample, L57-60; Methods / Data acquisition, L62-63

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The 130 healthy controls were used to train the Gaussian process regression normative model to predict voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) from age and sex. The trained model was then applied to 98 OCD patients to derive individualized deviations (Z-scores). Leave-one-out cross validation was performed on OCD patients to test model extendibility for inferring factor compositions.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Following the previous studies (Marquand et al. 2016; Wolfers et al. 2018), we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs and then applied the trained model to infer GMV of patients with OCD." "To examine the extendibility of our framework, we investigated whether the identified disease factors could be used to infer factor compositions of unseen patients using leave-one-out cross validation (LOOCV)."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling latent disease factors, L87-93; Methods / Examining the extendibility of our framework on unseen patients, L111-113

model-1.model-name: Gaussian process regression normative model for GMV

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was constructed using all 130 healthy controls. The paper does not describe a separate train/validation/test split for the normative model construction itself; all HCs were used for training the GPR model. The study uses a single-site design where all 130 HCs were used for model training.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "T1-weighted magnetic resonance images of 98 first-episode untreated patients with OCD and matched healthy controls (HCs, n = 130) were acquired." "we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs and then applied the trained model to infer GMV of patients with OCD."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The age statistics are provided directly in Table 1 for the HC group. Mean age was 20.046 years with SD 5.332. No range (min/max), median, or IQR values were reported in the paper. Since all 130 HCs were used for the normative model training without explicit train/validation split, the overall-phase and train-phase values are the same.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Results / Demographics and clinical characteristics, Table 1, L136-147

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Table 1 reports that 59 out of 130 HCs (45.38%) were male. The number of females is calculated by subtraction: 130 - 59 = 71 (54.62%). Since all 130 HCs were used for training the normative model without explicit splitting, overall-phase and train-phase values are identical. Percentages rounded: male 59/130 = 45.4%, female 71/130 = 54.6%.
